name: Tool - SNMP Tester
author: stephen
description: Creates and runs a temp script to troubleshoot SNMP credentials

nodeConfig.content:
Run this Playbook against a Linux host that netLD can log into.

It will create a temporary bash script in the host's /tmp directory and execute it.


The script will use some common SNMP commands included in most Linux hosts again the target device.


The target device to test must be entered as an IP address in the TARGET_IP variable in the Set Variables node.


The IP address of the netLD system must be placed in the NETLD_IP variable.


The script will query the netLD API for SNMP credentials that are already stored in netLD. You must first create an API token and paste the value in the API_TOKEN variable. You can delete your token after testing to ensure it is not used elsewhere by someone else.


The script will output the test results in standard output.


When complete, the script in the /tmp directory will be deleted.

block.commands:
rm -f /tmp/snmp_troubleshoot.sh
cat << 'EOF' > /tmp/snmp_troubleshoot.sh
#!/bin/bash
#
# SNMP Connectivity Troubleshooting Script
# 
# This script tests SNMP v1/v2c and v3 connectivity to a target device
# using credentials retrieved from a LogicVein/NetLD REST API.
#
# Required environment variables:
#   TARGET_IP   - IP address of the device to test
#   API_TOKEN   - Bearer token for REST API authentication
#
# Optional environment variables:
#   API_URL     - REST API URL (default: https://127.0.0.1/rest)
#   NETWORK     - Managed network name (default: Default)
#   SNMP_PORT   - SNMP port (default: 161)
#   TIMEOUT     - SNMP timeout in seconds (default: 5)
#   RETRIES     - Number of SNMP retries (default: 1)
#
# Dependencies: snmpget, curl, grep, sed, awk
#

set -o pipefail

# =============================================================================
# Configuration
# =============================================================================

# Required env vars
TARGET_IP="{TARGET_IP}"
API_TOKEN="{API_TOKEN}"

# Optional env vars with defaults
API_URL="https://{NETLD_IP}/rest"
NETWORK="Default"
SNMP_PORT=161
TIMEOUT=5
RETRIES=1

# Colors for output
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
BLUE='\033[0;34m'
CYAN='\033[0;36m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Test OID (sysDescr.0 - should be available on all SNMP-enabled devices)
TEST_OID=".1.3.6.1.2.1.1.1.0"

# =============================================================================
# Utility Functions
# =============================================================================

log_info() {
    printf "${BLUE}[INFO]${NC} %s\n" "$1" >&2
}

log_success() {
    printf "${GREEN}[SUCCESS]${NC} %s\n" "$1" >&2
}

log_warning() {
    printf "${YELLOW}[WARNING]${NC} %s\n" "$1" >&2
}

log_error() {
    printf "${RED}[ERROR]${NC} %s\n" "$1" >&2
}

log_debug() {
    printf "${CYAN}[DEBUG]${NC} %s\n" "$1" >&2
}

log_header() {
    printf "\n" >&2
    printf "${CYAN}-----------------------------------------------------------------${NC}\n" >&2
    printf "${CYAN} %s${NC}\n" "$1" >&2
    printf "${CYAN}-----------------------------------------------------------------${NC}\n" >&2
}

log_subheader() {
    printf "\n" >&2
    printf "${BLUE}--- %s ---${NC}\n" "$1" >&2
}

# Print to stdout (for user-facing output that's not log messages)
print_output() {
    printf "%s\n" "$1"
}

# Check if a command exists
check_command() {
    if ! command -v "$1" &> /dev/null; then
        log_error "Required command '$1' is not installed"
        return 1
    fi
    return 0
}

# =============================================================================
# JSON Parsing Functions (no jq required)
# =============================================================================

# Extract a simple string value from JSON by key
# Usage: json_get_value "$json" "keyname"
json_get_value() {
    local json="$1"
    local key="$2"
    printf '%s' "$json" | grep -o "\"$key\"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*\"[^\"]*\"" | head -1 | sed "s/\"$key\"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*\"//" | sed 's/"$//'
}

# Extract a value that might be a string or other type
# Usage: json_get_any_value "$json" "keyname"
json_get_any_value() {
    local json="$1"
    local key="$2"
    # Try string first
    local val
    val=$(json_get_value "$json" "$key")
    if [[ -n "$val" ]]; then
        printf '%s' "$val"
        return
    fi
    # Try non-string (number, boolean, null)
    printf '%s' "$json" | grep -o "\"$key\"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*[^,}]*" | head -1 | sed "s/\"$key\"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*//" | sed 's/[[:space:]]*$//'
}

# Extract all values for a given key from a JSON array
# Usage: json_get_all_values "$json" "keyname"
json_get_all_values() {
    local json="$1"
    local key="$2"
    printf '%s' "$json" | grep -o "\"$key\"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*\"[^\"]*\"" | sed "s/\"$key\"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*\"//" | sed 's/"$//'
}

# Check if JSON response contains an error
# Usage: json_has_error "$json"
json_has_error() {
    local json="$1"
    if printf '%s' "$json" | grep -q '"error"[[:space:]]*:'; then
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

# Get error message from JSON-RPC response
# Usage: json_get_error "$json"
json_get_error() {
    local json="$1"
    json_get_value "$json" "message"
}

# Extract credential sets array and parse each one
# This function outputs one credential set per line in format:
# name|roCommunityString|snmpUsername|snmpAuthPassword|snmpPrivPassword
parse_credential_sets() {
    local json="$1"
    
    # Split by credential set boundaries and process each
    printf '%s' "$json" | tr '{}' '\n' | while read -r chunk; do
        # Check if this chunk has credential data
        if printf '%s' "$chunk" | grep -q '"name"[[:space:]]*:'; then
            local name ro_community snmp_user snmp_auth snmp_priv
            
            name=$(json_get_value "$chunk" "name")
            ro_community=$(json_get_value "$chunk" "roCommunityString")
            snmp_user=$(json_get_value "$chunk" "snmpUsername")
            snmp_auth=$(json_get_value "$chunk" "snmpAuthPassword")
            snmp_priv=$(json_get_value "$chunk" "snmpPrivPassword")
            
            # Only output if we got a name (indicates valid credential set)
            if [[ -n "$name" ]]; then
                printf '%s|%s|%s|%s|%s\n' "$name" "$ro_community" "$snmp_user" "$snmp_auth" "$snmp_priv"
            fi
        fi
    done
}

# Extract SNMP protocol properties (auth and encryption settings)
# Usage: parse_snmp_protocol_config "$json"
# Returns: auth_protocol|priv_protocol
parse_snmp_protocol_config() {
    local json="$1"
    local auth_proto="MD5"
    local priv_proto="DES"
    
    # Find SNMP section and extract V3 Authentication and V3 Encryption values
    if printf '%s' "$json" | grep -q '"name"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"SNMP"'; then
        # Look for V3 Authentication
        local auth_val
        auth_val=$(printf '%s' "$json" | grep -o '"key"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"V3 Authentication"[^}]*"value"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"[^"]*"' | grep -o '"value"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"[^"]*"' | sed 's/"value"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"//' | sed 's/"$//')
        [[ -n "$auth_val" ]] && auth_proto="$auth_val"
        
        # Look for V3 Encryption
        local priv_val
        priv_val=$(printf '%s' "$json" | grep -o '"key"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"V3 Encryption"[^}]*"value"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"[^"]*"' | grep -o '"value"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"[^"]*"' | sed 's/"value"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"//' | sed 's/"$//')
        [[ -n "$priv_val" ]] && priv_proto="$priv_val"
    fi
    
    printf '%s|%s' "$auth_proto" "$priv_proto"
}

# =============================================================================
# Prerequisite Checks
# =============================================================================

check_prerequisites() {
    log_header "Checking Prerequisites"
    
    local missing_deps=0
    
    # Check required commands
    for cmd in snmpget curl grep sed awk; do
        if check_command "$cmd"; then
            log_success "$cmd is available"
        else
            missing_deps=1
        fi
    done
    
    # Check required environment variables
    if [[ -z "$TARGET_IP" ]]; then
        log_error "TARGET_IP environment variable is not set"
        missing_deps=1
    else
        log_success "TARGET_IP is set: $TARGET_IP"
    fi
    
    if [[ -z "$API_TOKEN" ]]; then
        log_error "API_TOKEN environment variable is not set"
        missing_deps=1
    else
        log_success "API_TOKEN is set: [REDACTED]"
    fi
    
    # Validate IP address format
    if [[ -n "$TARGET_IP" ]] && ! [[ "$TARGET_IP" =~ ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ ]]; then
        log_error "TARGET_IP '$TARGET_IP' does not appear to be a valid IPv4 address"
        missing_deps=1
    fi
    
    if [[ $missing_deps -eq 1 ]]; then
        log_error "Prerequisites check failed. Please install missing dependencies and set required environment variables."
        exit 1
    fi
    
    log_success "All prerequisites satisfied"
}

# =============================================================================
# Network Connectivity Tests
# =============================================================================

test_basic_connectivity() {
    log_header "Testing Basic Network Connectivity"
    
    # Test ICMP ping
    log_subheader "ICMP Ping Test"
    if ping -c 3 -W 2 "$TARGET_IP" &> /dev/null; then
        log_success "Host $TARGET_IP is reachable via ICMP"
    else
        log_warning "Host $TARGET_IP does not respond to ICMP ping (may be blocked by firewall)"
    fi
    
    # Test UDP port connectivity using nc if available
    log_subheader "SNMP Port Test (UDP $SNMP_PORT)"
    if command -v nc &> /dev/null; then
        if nc -zu -w 2 "$TARGET_IP" "$SNMP_PORT" 2>/dev/null; then
            log_success "UDP port $SNMP_PORT appears to be open"
        else
            log_warning "Cannot confirm UDP port $SNMP_PORT is open (this is normal for UDP)"
        fi
    else
        log_info "netcat (nc) not available - skipping port test"
    fi
    
    # Check if we can reach the API
    log_subheader "API Connectivity Test"
    local api_response
    api_response=$(curl -sk -w "%{http_code}" -o /dev/null \
        -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_TOKEN" \
        -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
        "$API_URL" 2>&1)
    
    if [[ "$api_response" == "200" ]] || [[ "$api_response" == "404" ]] || [[ "$api_response" == "405" ]]; then
        log_success "API endpoint is reachable (HTTP $api_response)"
    else
        log_error "Cannot reach API endpoint at $API_URL (HTTP $api_response)"
        log_error "Please verify API_URL and API_TOKEN are correct"
        exit 1
    fi
}

# =============================================================================
# REST API Functions
# =============================================================================

api_call() {
    local payload="$1"
    local response
    
    response=$(curl -sk \
        -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_TOKEN" \
        -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
        -d "$payload" \
        "$API_URL" 2>&1)
    
    local curl_exit=$?
    
    if [[ $curl_exit -ne 0 ]]; then
        log_error "curl failed with exit code $curl_exit"
        return 1
    fi
    
    # Check for JSON-RPC error
    if json_has_error "$response"; then
        local error_msg
        error_msg=$(json_get_error "$response")
        log_error "API returned error: $error_msg"
        return 1
    fi
    
    printf '%s' "$response"
}

get_credential_configs() {
    local payload
    payload=$(printf '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"Credentials.getAllCredentialConfigs","params":{"network":"%s"},"id":1}' "$NETWORK")
    
    local response
    response=$(api_call "$payload")
    
    if [[ -z "$response" ]]; then
        log_error "Failed to fetch credential configurations"
        return 1
    fi
    
    # Extract config names using our JSON parser
    local config_names
    config_names=$(json_get_all_values "$response" "name")
    
    if [[ -z "$config_names" ]]; then
        log_warning "No credential configurations found"
        return 1
    fi
    
    printf '%s' "$config_names"
}

get_credential_sets() {
    local config_name="$1"
    
    local payload
    payload=$(printf '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"Credentials.getCredentialSets","params":{"pageData":{"offset":0,"pageSize":1000,"total":0,"credentialSets":[]},"network":"%s","configName":"%s","ipOrCidr":null,"sortColumn":"ipAddress","descending":false},"id":1}' "$NETWORK" "$config_name")
    
    local response
    response=$(api_call "$payload")
    
    if [[ -z "$response" ]]; then
        return 1
    fi
    
    printf '%s' "$response"
}

get_protocol_configs() {
    local payload
    payload=$(printf '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"Credentials.getAllProtocolConfigs","params":{"network":"%s"},"id":1}' "$NETWORK")
    
    local response
    response=$(api_call "$payload")
    
    if [[ -z "$response" ]]; then
        log_error "Failed to fetch protocol configurations"
        return 1
    fi
    
    printf '%s' "$response"
}

# =============================================================================
# SNMP Testing Functions
# =============================================================================

# Map auth protocol name to snmp command option
get_auth_protocol() {
    local proto="$1"
    case "${proto^^}" in
        "MD5")  printf 'MD5' ;;
        "SHA")  printf 'SHA' ;;
        "SHA-224"|"SHA224") printf 'SHA-224' ;;
        "SHA-256"|"SHA256") printf 'SHA-256' ;;
        "SHA-384"|"SHA384") printf 'SHA-384' ;;
        "SHA-512"|"SHA512") printf 'SHA-512' ;;
        *)      printf 'MD5' ;;
    esac
}

# Map priv protocol name to snmp command option
get_priv_protocol() {
    local proto="$1"
    case "${proto^^}" in
        "DES")      printf 'DES' ;;
        "AES"|"AES128"|"AES-128") printf 'AES' ;;
        "AES192"|"AES-192") printf 'AES-192' ;;
        "AES256"|"AES-256") printf 'AES-256' ;;
        "3DES")     printf '3DES' ;;
        *)          printf 'DES' ;;
    esac
}

# Analyze SNMP error and provide detailed feedback
analyze_snmp_error() {
    local error_output="$1"
    local version="$2"
    local credential_info="$3"
    
    printf "\n" >&2
    log_debug "Analyzing error output..."
    
    if printf '%s' "$error_output" | grep -qi "timeout"; then
        log_error "SNMP Timeout"
        printf "  Possible causes:\n" >&2
        printf "    - Host is not reachable on UDP port %s\n" "$SNMP_PORT" >&2
        printf "    - SNMP service is not running on the target device\n" >&2
        printf "    - Firewall is blocking SNMP traffic\n" >&2
        printf "    - Wrong IP address\n" >&2
        printf "  Troubleshooting steps:\n" >&2
        printf "    1. Verify the target IP address is correct\n" >&2
        printf "    2. Check if SNMP is enabled on the target device\n" >&2
        printf "    3. Verify firewall rules allow UDP port %s\n" "$SNMP_PORT" >&2
        printf "    4. Try increasing the timeout value\n" >&2
        
    elif printf '%s' "$error_output" | grep -qi "no response"; then
        log_error "No Response from Agent"
        printf "  Possible causes:\n" >&2
        printf "    - SNMP agent is not running\n" >&2
        printf "    - Network connectivity issues\n" >&2
        printf "    - SNMP requests are being filtered\n" >&2
        printf "  Troubleshooting steps:\n" >&2
        printf "    1. Verify SNMP service status on target device\n" >&2
        printf "    2. Check network path for packet loss\n" >&2
        
    elif printf '%s' "$error_output" | grep -qi "authentication failure\|authorizationError"; then
        log_error "Authentication Failure"
        printf "  Possible causes:\n" >&2
        if [[ "$version" == "3" ]]; then
            printf "    - Incorrect SNMPv3 username\n" >&2
            printf "    - Wrong authentication password\n" >&2
            printf "    - Mismatched authentication protocol (MD5/SHA)\n" >&2
            printf "  Troubleshooting steps:\n" >&2
            printf "    1. Verify SNMPv3 user exists on target device\n" >&2
            printf "    2. Confirm authentication password matches\n" >&2
            printf "    3. Check authentication protocol setting\n" >&2
        else
            printf "    - Community string does not match\n" >&2
            printf "    - Community string has restricted access\n" >&2
            printf "  Troubleshooting steps:\n" >&2
            printf "    1. Verify community string is correct\n" >&2
            printf "    2. Check if community string has read access\n" >&2
            printf "    3. Verify source IP is allowed to query\n" >&2
        fi
        
    elif printf '%s' "$error_output" | grep -qi "unknown user name\|unknownUserName"; then
        log_error "Unknown User Name"
        printf "  Possible causes:\n" >&2
        printf "    - SNMPv3 user '%s' does not exist on target\n" "$credential_info" >&2
        printf "    - User name is case-sensitive and may not match\n" >&2
        printf "  Troubleshooting steps:\n" >&2
        printf "    1. Verify the SNMPv3 user is configured on the device\n" >&2
        printf "    2. Check for case sensitivity in the user name\n" >&2
        
    elif printf '%s' "$error_output" | grep -qi "decryption error\|decryptionError"; then
        log_error "Decryption Error"
        printf "  Possible causes:\n" >&2
        printf "    - Wrong privacy password\n" >&2
        printf "    - Mismatched encryption protocol (DES/AES)\n" >&2
        printf "    - Privacy protocol not supported by agent\n" >&2
        printf "  Troubleshooting steps:\n" >&2
        printf "    1. Verify privacy password matches device configuration\n" >&2
        printf "    2. Check encryption protocol matches (DES/AES/AES256)\n" >&2
        printf "    3. Ensure target device supports the encryption protocol\n" >&2
        
    elif printf '%s' "$error_output" | grep -qi "unsupportedSecLevel\|unsupported security level"; then
        log_error "Unsupported Security Level"
        printf "  Possible causes:\n" >&2
        printf "    - Target device doesn't support requested security level\n" >&2
        printf "    - User not configured for authPriv level\n" >&2
        printf "  Troubleshooting steps:\n" >&2
        printf "    1. Check user's security level configuration on device\n" >&2
        printf "    2. Try lower security level (authNoPriv or noAuthNoPriv)\n" >&2
        
    elif printf '%s' "$error_output" | grep -qi "no such object\|noSuchObject"; then
        log_warning "No Such Object (but SNMP is working!)"
        printf "  This actually indicates SNMP connectivity is successful!\n" >&2
        printf "  The OID requested simply doesn't exist on this device.\n" >&2
        return 0
        
    elif printf '%s' "$error_output" | grep -qi "no access\|noAccess"; then
        log_error "No Access"
        printf "  Possible causes:\n" >&2
        printf "    - SNMP view restricts access to requested OID\n" >&2
        printf "    - Access control list denies this request\n" >&2
        printf "  Note: SNMP connectivity is working, but access is restricted\n" >&2
        
    elif printf '%s' "$error_output" | grep -qi "generic error\|genError"; then
        log_error "Generic SNMP Error"
        printf "  The SNMP agent returned a generic error.\n" >&2
        printf "  This usually indicates a problem on the agent side.\n" >&2
        
    elif printf '%s' "$error_output" | grep -qi "bad version\|version"; then
        log_error "SNMP Version Mismatch"
        printf "  Possible causes:\n" >&2
        printf "    - Target device doesn't support SNMP %s\n" "$version" >&2
        printf "    - SNMP version disabled on target\n" >&2
        printf "  Troubleshooting steps:\n" >&2
        printf "    1. Verify which SNMP versions are enabled on target\n" >&2
        printf "    2. Try a different SNMP version\n" >&2
        
    elif printf '%s' "$error_output" | grep -qi "connection refused"; then
        log_error "Connection Refused"
        printf "  Possible causes:\n" >&2
        printf "    - SNMP service not running on target\n" >&2
        printf "    - Port %s is not listening\n" "$SNMP_PORT" >&2
        
    else
        log_error "Unknown Error"
        printf "  Raw error output:\n" >&2
        printf "  %s\n" "$error_output" >&2
        printf "\n" >&2
        printf "  General troubleshooting steps:\n" >&2
        printf "    1. Verify network connectivity to target\n" >&2
        printf "    2. Confirm SNMP is enabled on target device\n" >&2
        printf "    3. Check credential configuration\n" >&2
    fi
    
    return 1
}

# Test SNMP v1
test_snmpv1() {
    local community="$1"
    local cred_name="$2"
    
    log_info "Testing SNMPv1 with community string from '$cred_name'..."
    
    local output
    output=$(snmpget -v1 -c "$community" -t "$TIMEOUT" -r "$RETRIES" \
        "$TARGET_IP:$SNMP_PORT" "$TEST_OID" 2>&1)
    local exit_code=$?
    
    if [[ $exit_code -eq 0 ]]; then
        log_success "SNMPv1 successful!"
        printf "  Response: %s\n" "$output" >&2
        return 0
    else
        log_error "SNMPv1 failed"
        analyze_snmp_error "$output" "1" "$community"
        return 1
    fi
}

# Test SNMP v2c
test_snmpv2c() {
    local community="$1"
    local cred_name="$2"
    
    log_info "Testing SNMPv2c with community string from '$cred_name'..."
    
    local output
    output=$(snmpget -v2c -c "$community" -t "$TIMEOUT" -r "$RETRIES" \
        "$TARGET_IP:$SNMP_PORT" "$TEST_OID" 2>&1)
    local exit_code=$?
    
    if [[ $exit_code -eq 0 ]]; then
        log_success "SNMPv2c successful!"
        printf "  Response: %s\n" "$output" >&2
        return 0
    else
        log_error "SNMPv2c failed"
        analyze_snmp_error "$output" "2c" "$community"
        return 1
    fi
}

# Test SNMP v3
test_snmpv3() {
    local username="$1"
    local auth_pass="$2"
    local priv_pass="$3"
    local auth_proto="$4"
    local priv_proto="$5"
    local cred_name="$6"
    
    # Map protocol names
    auth_proto=$(get_auth_protocol "$auth_proto")
    priv_proto=$(get_priv_protocol "$priv_proto")
    
    local sec_level
    local snmp_cmd
    
    if [[ -n "$auth_pass" ]] && [[ -n "$priv_pass" ]]; then
        sec_level="authPriv"
        log_info "Testing SNMPv3 (authPriv) user '$username' from '$cred_name'..."
        log_debug "Using auth=$auth_proto, priv=$priv_proto"
        
        snmp_cmd="snmpget -v3 -l authPriv -u $username \
            -a $auth_proto -A $auth_pass \
            -x $priv_proto -X $priv_pass \
            -t $TIMEOUT -r $RETRIES \
            $TARGET_IP:$SNMP_PORT $TEST_OID"
            
    elif [[ -n "$auth_pass" ]]; then
        sec_level="authNoPriv"
        log_info "Testing SNMPv3 (authNoPriv) user '$username' from '$cred_name'..."
        log_debug "Using auth=$auth_proto"
        
        snmp_cmd="snmpget -v3 -l authNoPriv -u $username \
            -a $auth_proto -A $auth_pass \
            -t $TIMEOUT -r $RETRIES \
            $TARGET_IP:$SNMP_PORT $TEST_OID"
            
    else
        sec_level="noAuthNoPriv"
        log_info "Testing SNMPv3 (noAuthNoPriv) user '$username' from '$cred_name'..."
        
        snmp_cmd="snmpget -v3 -l noAuthNoPriv -u $username \
            -t $TIMEOUT -r $RETRIES \
            $TARGET_IP:$SNMP_PORT $TEST_OID"
    fi
    
    local output
    output=$(eval "$snmp_cmd" 2>&1)
    local exit_code=$?
    
    if [[ $exit_code -eq 0 ]]; then
        log_success "SNMPv3 ($sec_level) successful!"
        printf "  Response: %s\n" "$output" >&2
        return 0
    else
        log_error "SNMPv3 ($sec_level) failed"
        analyze_snmp_error "$output" "3" "$username"
        return 1
    fi
}

# =============================================================================
# Main Testing Logic
# =============================================================================

run_snmp_tests() {
    log_header "Retrieving Credentials from API"
    
    # Get protocol configurations for auth/priv settings
    log_subheader "Fetching Protocol Configurations"
    local proto_response
    proto_response=$(get_protocol_configs)
    
    # Extract SNMP auth and priv protocols from response
    local snmp_auth_proto="MD5"
    local snmp_priv_proto="DES"
    
    if [[ -n "$proto_response" ]]; then
        local proto_config
        proto_config=$(parse_snmp_protocol_config "$proto_response")
        snmp_auth_proto=$(printf '%s' "$proto_config" | cut -d'|' -f1)
        snmp_priv_proto=$(printf '%s' "$proto_config" | cut -d'|' -f2)
        log_info "SNMP Protocol Config: Auth=$snmp_auth_proto, Priv=$snmp_priv_proto"
    else
        log_warning "Could not fetch protocol config, using defaults: Auth=MD5, Priv=DES"
    fi
    
    # Get credential configurations
    log_subheader "Fetching Credential Configurations"
    local config_names
    config_names=$(get_credential_configs)
    
    if [[ -z "$config_names" ]]; then
        log_error "No credential configurations found. Cannot proceed with testing."
        exit 1
    fi
    
    log_info "Found credential configurations:"
    printf '%s\n' "$config_names" | while read -r name; do
        [[ -n "$name" ]] && printf "  - %s\n" "$name" >&2
    done
    
    # Track test results using temp files
    local success_file counts_file
    success_file=$(mktemp)
    counts_file=$(mktemp)
    printf '0|0|0|0|0' > "$counts_file"
    
    log_header "Running SNMP Tests"
    
    # Loop through each credential configuration
    printf '%s\n' "$config_names" | while IFS= read -r config_name; do
        # Skip empty lines
        [[ -z "$config_name" ]] && continue
        
        log_subheader "Processing Credential Config: $config_name"
        
        local cred_sets_response
        cred_sets_response=$(get_credential_sets "$config_name")
        
        if [[ -z "$cred_sets_response" ]]; then
            log_warning "No credential sets found in '$config_name'"
            continue
        fi
        
        # Parse credential sets
        local parsed_creds
        parsed_creds=$(parse_credential_sets "$cred_sets_response")
        
        if [[ -z "$parsed_creds" ]]; then
            log_warning "No credential sets in '$config_name'"
            continue
        fi
        
        local cred_count
        cred_count=$(printf '%s\n' "$parsed_creds" | wc -l)
        log_info "Found $cred_count credential set(s) in '$config_name'"
        
        # Process each credential set
        printf '%s\n' "$parsed_creds" | while IFS='|' read -r cred_name ro_community snmp_user snmp_auth snmp_priv; do
            [[ -z "$cred_name" ]] && continue
            
            printf "\n" >&2
            log_info "Testing credential set: '$cred_name' (Config: $config_name)"
            
            # Read current counts
            local total_tests successful_tests v1_success v2c_success v3_success
            IFS='|' read -r total_tests successful_tests v1_success v2c_success v3_success < "$counts_file"
            
            # Test SNMP v1/v2c if community string is available
            if [[ -n "$ro_community" ]]; then
                printf "\n" >&2
                # Test SNMPv1
                total_tests=$((total_tests + 1))
                if test_snmpv1 "$ro_community" "$cred_name"; then
                    successful_tests=$((successful_tests + 1))
                    v1_success=$((v1_success + 1))
                    printf 'SNMPv1: %s (Config: %s)\n' "$cred_name" "$config_name" >> "$success_file"
                fi
                
                printf "\n" >&2
                # Test SNMPv2c
                total_tests=$((total_tests + 1))
                if test_snmpv2c "$ro_community" "$cred_name"; then
                    successful_tests=$((successful_tests + 1))
                    v2c_success=$((v2c_success + 1))
                    printf 'SNMPv2c: %s (Config: %s)\n' "$cred_name" "$config_name" >> "$success_file"
                fi
            else
                log_warning "No community string in '$cred_name' - skipping v1/v2c tests"
            fi
            
            # Test SNMP v3 if username is available
            if [[ -n "$snmp_user" ]]; then
                printf "\n" >&2
                total_tests=$((total_tests + 1))
                if test_snmpv3 "$snmp_user" "$snmp_auth" "$snmp_priv" \
                    "$snmp_auth_proto" "$snmp_priv_proto" "$cred_name"; then
                    successful_tests=$((successful_tests + 1))
                    v3_success=$((v3_success + 1))
                    printf 'SNMPv3: %s (User: %s, Config: %s)\n' "$cred_name" "$snmp_user" "$config_name" >> "$success_file"
                fi
            else
                log_warning "No SNMPv3 username in '$cred_name' - skipping v3 tests"
            fi
            
            # Save counts
            printf '%s|%s|%s|%s|%s' "$total_tests" "$successful_tests" "$v1_success" "$v2c_success" "$v3_success" > "$counts_file"
            
        done
        
    done
    
    # Read final counts
    local total_tests successful_tests v1_success v2c_success v3_success
    IFS='|' read -r total_tests successful_tests v1_success v2c_success v3_success < "$counts_file"
    
    # Print summary
    log_header "Test Summary"
    
    printf "Target: %s:%s\n" "$TARGET_IP" "$SNMP_PORT" >&2
    printf "Network: %s\n" "$NETWORK" >&2
    printf "\n" >&2
    printf "Total tests run: %s\n" "$total_tests" >&2
    printf "Successful: %s\n" "$successful_tests" >&2
    printf "Failed: %s\n" "$((total_tests - successful_tests))" >&2
    printf "\n" >&2
    printf "By version:\n" >&2
    printf "  SNMPv1:  %s successful\n" "$v1_success" >&2
    printf "  SNMPv2c: %s successful\n" "$v2c_success" >&2
    printf "  SNMPv3:  %s successful\n" "$v3_success" >&2
    
    if [[ -s "$success_file" ]]; then
        printf "\n" >&2
        log_success "Working credentials:"
        while read -r cred; do
            printf "  ✓ %s\n" "$cred" >&2
        done < "$success_file"
    else
        printf "\n" >&2
        log_error "No working SNMP credentials found!"
        printf "\n" >&2
        printf "Recommendations:\n" >&2
        printf "  1. Verify the target device has SNMP enabled\n" >&2
        printf "  2. Check firewall rules for UDP port %s\n" "$SNMP_PORT" >&2
        printf "  3. Verify credential configurations in the management system\n" >&2
        printf "  4. Ensure the target IP is correct\n" >&2
        printf "  5. Check if SNMP access control lists (ACLs) allow this source\n" >&2
    fi
    
    # Cleanup temp files
    rm -f "$success_file" "$counts_file"
    
    # Return appropriate exit code
    if [[ $successful_tests -gt 0 ]]; then
        return 0
    else
        return 1
    fi
}

# Main Entry Point
# =============================================================================

main() {
    printf "\n" >&2
    printf "${CYAN}-----------------------------------------------------------------${NC}\n" >&2
    printf "${CYAN}         SNMP Connectivity Troubleshooting Script                ${NC}\n" >&2
    printf "${CYAN}-----------------------------------------------------------------${NC}\n" >&2
    printf "\n" >&2
    
    log_info "Script started at $(date)"
    log_info "Target: ${TARGET_IP:-NOT SET}"
    log_info "API URL: $API_URL"
    log_info "Network: $NETWORK"
    
    check_prerequisites
    test_basic_connectivity
    run_snmp_tests
    exit_code=$?
    
    printf "\n" >&2
    log_info "Script completed at $(date)"
    
    exit $exit_code
}

main "$@"
